requested_by: Natalie Brooks, Security Awareness Program Lead
title: Phishing test PH-2026-Q4 results: who clicked, who gave up a password, what next
situation: We ran a simulated phishing email for 12 employees in Finance, Engineering, Sales and HR. Two people entered their passwords on the fake page, and three clicked the link. We also have five unusual behaviour reports, like an admin stopping security software, and four real emails users forwarded for a verdict.
your_task: Give each employee a follow-up action based on their result, role risk, repeat failures and training record.
Calculate click, password-entry and report rates by department and for the whole program, against targets.
Classify the five behaviour reports and pick a response and a technical control for each.
Score the four forwarded emails on phishing signs and mark each one REPORT_AS_PHISHING or LIKELY_SAFE.
why_it_matters: A password typed into a fake page is a real account compromise until it is reset. Departments that handle money, like Finance, are the main targets for invoice and payment fraud.
done_when: All 12 employees have an action and the rule that triggered it.
Department and program metrics are reported, with Finance, HR and Sales flagged.
The two password submitters (E03, E08) are sent to the Identity and Access Management (IAM) team for a forced password reset, session revocation and a check of multi-factor authentication (MFA).
Both risky behaviours (B1, B4) are referred to the insider-threat team.

glossary.Phishing simulation: A safe, fake phishing email sent to staff to measure and train their responses.
glossary.Credential submission: Typing a username and password into the fake page; in real life, the account would be compromised.
glossary.Report rate: The share of people who reported the email to security.
glossary.BEC (business email compromise): A scam that uses fake or hijacked business email to get payments or data.
glossary.Typosquatting: Using a look-alike domain, like examp1e.com, to trick people.
glossary.UEBA: User and entity behaviour analytics: tools that flag activity unusual for a person or device.

talking_point: Analyzed a 12-person phishing test with a 41.7% click rate and 16.7% password-entry rate, flagged 3 of 4 departments, sent the 2 compromised users to IAM for forced resets and session revocation, and flagged 2 of 4 forwarded emails as phishing.
